(a) It is unlawful for any person to keep any hogs, cattle, sheep, goats, horses, mules, poultry or any other such animals for commercial purposes.
(b) It is unlawful for any person to keep any hogs, cattle, sheep, goats, horses, mules or any other such animal in a shed, pen, stall or other such structure within 400 feet of any residence or within 500 feet of any public street in the city.
(c) Backyard poultry.
Definitions:
Coop: An enclosed, covered structure designed to house poultry.
Poultry: For purposes of this ordinance, "poultry" refers to chickens, quail and pigeons raised for eggs, meat, or as pets.
Run: A secure, enclosed outdoor area attached to a coop where poultry can exercise.
Backyard poultry are for non-commercial use only. Poultry, poultry products, and/or by-products shall not be sold on the property.
Permitted birds:
Chickens, quail and pigeons
Prohibited birds:
Ducks, turkey, geese, peacocks, and roosters. This prohibition shall not apply to ducks or other waterfowl inhabiting natural or manmade watercourses or bodies of water.
Maximum number of birds allowed:
(1) For property under one acre, up to six birds are permitted. For property over one acre, six additional birds are permitted per acre.
a. The maximum number of birds may consist of a combination of allowable birds.
(2) A maximum of 12 backyard chickens are allowed in a residential district.
Zoning and property requirements:
(1) Chickens shall only be allowed on single-family residential lots containing a maximum of one residence.
(2) Henhouses, coops, and chicken tractors shall be restricted to the backyard area of a single-family residential lot and must be contained within the yard of the residence.
(3) The keeping of chickens and other allowed birds is only permitted in areas zoned R1 (single-family residential).
Coop and run requirements:
(1) Flight prevention: The primary flight feathers on the wings must be clipped to prevent flight.
(2) Coop Size: A coop is required to house the chickens. The coop must provide at least three square feet of space per chicken, with a minimum of 18 inches of overhead space per level of the coop.
(3) Run Size: An area outside of the coop must be provided as a run. The run requires a minimum of nine square feet per chicken.
(4) Containment: The coop and run must be fully contained within the property.
(5) Setbacks: Coops and runs must be located at least ten feet from any property line and 30 feet residential structures on neighboring parcels.
(6) Fencing: Runs must be enclosed with fencing to prevent birds from straying from the property of the owner or keeper, or going upon the property of another person or public rights-of-way.
Maintenance and sanitation:
(1) Coops and runs must be kept clean and free of debris, manure, rodents, insects, parasites, and other waste.
(2) Bedding material must be replaced regularly to prevent odor and the attraction of pests.
(3) Feed must be stored in secure containers to prevent access by rodents and other wildlife.
Noise control:
(1) Birds should be kept in a manner that does not create a nuisance to neighbors.
(2) Any excessive noise complaints may result in an inspection and possible reduction in the number of birds allowed.
Health and safety:
(1) Birds must be provided with adequate food, water, shelter, and veterinary care.
(2) Dead birds must be disposed of in a sanitary manner and in accordance with local regulations.
Permit and inspection:
All backyard growers must register their flock with the City of Lavonia by giving their name, address, telephone number, and number and type of chickens. This registration is mandatory and shall be free of charge. Early identification of all domestic birds in the area is essential to containment procedures in the event of an avian influenza outbreak.
All flocks located within the city limits are subject to inspection by the City of Lavonia or its designee.
Prohibited activities:
(1) The slaughtering of birds for personal use must be done in a humane and private manner, out of public view.
(2) The sale of eggs or birds from residential properties is prohibited unless the resident obtains a business license and complies with all zoning and health regulations.
Violations and penalties:
Failure to comply with the provisions of this ordinance may result in fines, revocation of the permit, and the removal of the birds from the property.
(Code 1995, § 6.04.020; Ord. of 11-4-2024(1), § I)
